songs.title: Alouette
songs.attribution: French-Canadian traditional children's song, first printed in A Pocket Song Book for the Use of Students and Graduates of McGill College (Montreal, 1879); anonymous, public domain.

songs.title: Amazing Grace
songs.attribution: Words by John Newton (Olney Hymns, 1779); the tune "New Britain" is an American folk melody first printed in 1829 and joined to Newton's text in William Walker's Southern Harmony (1835), so both are public domain worldwide.

songs.title: Arirang
songs.attribution: Traditional Korean folk song (the "Bonjo Arirang" of Gyeonggi), transcribed by Homer Hulbert in 1896; melody and words are anonymous and public domain. Written in 9/8 with the eighth note as the beat (dotted quarter = 3 beats), so the tempo is in eighths (about 50 dotted quarters per minute).

songs.title: Au clair de la lune
songs.attribution: French traditional children's song, melody and words from the 18th century (the words are sometimes attributed to Lully, 17th century); anonymous, public domain.

songs.title: Auld Lang Syne
songs.attribution: Words by Robert Burns (1788), sung to the traditional Scots tune first paired with the text in George Thomson's Select Songs of Scotland (1799); both are public domain worldwide.

songs.title: Aura Lee
songs.attribution: Music by George R. Poulton (1828-1867), words by W. W. Fosdick (1825-1862), published in Cincinnati in 1861 (the tune later used for "Love Me Tender"); public domain.

songs.title: Beautiful Dreamer
songs.attribution: Words and music by Stephen C. Foster (1826-1864), published posthumously by Wm. A. Pond & Co., New York, in 1864; public domain. Written in 9/8 with the eighth note as the beat (dotted quarter = 3 beats), so the tempo is in eighths (about 63 dotted quarters per minute). The C# is Foster's chromatic lower neighbour.

songs.title: Bella Ciao
songs.attribution: Italian folk melody (older than the words, related to a 19th-century mondina work song); the partisan words are anonymous, from the 1940s, first published in 1953 (Canti della Resistenza italiana). Anonymous and traditional, public domain.

songs.title: Brahms' Lullaby (Wiegenlied)
songs.attribution: Melody: "Wiegenlied" Op. 49 No. 4 by Johannes Brahms (1868); the English words "Lullaby and good night" are the traditional 19th-century translation. Both are public domain worldwide.

songs.title: Feel (Stripped)
songs.attribution: "Feel (Stripped)" by Cortez, licensed CC BY 4.0. Recording from Jamendo (https://www.jamendo.com/track/1481500/feel-stripped); word timings from the JamendoLyrics dataset.

songs.title: Danny Boy
songs.attribution: The melody is the traditional Irish "Londonderry Air" (first printed by George Petrie in 1855); the words were written by Frederic Weatherly in 1913 (he died in 1929), so both are public domain worldwide.

songs.title: Deck the Halls
songs.attribution: Melody: the 16th-century Welsh New Year's tune "Nos Galan"; English words by Thomas Oliphant (1862). Both are public domain worldwide.

songs.title: Down by the Riverside
songs.attribution: African-American spiritual, sung since before the Civil War and first published in Plantation Melodies (1918); anonymous, public domain. The A# is the traditional chromatic lower neighbour in "down by the riverside".

songs.title: Freifliegen
songs.attribution: "Freifliegen" by Durch Dick und Dünn, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Recording from Jamendo (https://www.jamendo.com/track/34276/freifliegen/lyrics); word timings from the JamendoLyrics dataset.

songs.title: l'abandon
songs.attribution: "l'abandon" by FLO, licensed CC BY 4.0. Recording from Jamendo (https://www.jamendo.com/track/48843/l-abandon/lyrics); word timings from the JamendoLyrics dataset.

songs.title: For He's a Jolly Good Fellow
songs.attribution: Melody: the French song "Marlbrough s'en va-t-en guerre" (18th century); the English congratulatory words are 19th-century traditional. Both are public domain worldwide.

songs.title: Frère Jacques
songs.attribution: Traditional French nursery round, words and melody in print by the late 18th century; public domain worldwide.

songs.title: Funiculì, Funiculà
songs.attribution: Music by Luigi Denza (1846-1922), Neapolitan words by Peppino Turco (1846-1903), written in 1880 for the opening of the Vesuvius funicular; both authors died more than 70 years ago, public domain. Written in 6/8 with the eighth note as the beat (dotted quarter = 3 beats), so the tempo is in eighths (about 100 dotted quarters per minute).

songs.title: Good King Wenceslas
songs.attribution: Melody: the 13th-century spring carol "Tempus adest floridum" (printed in Piae Cantiones, 1582); words by John Mason Neale (1853). Both are public domain worldwide.

songs.title: Greensleeves
songs.attribution: Traditional English tune and words, registered at the Stationers' Company in 1580 and printed in A Handful of Pleasant Delights (1584); public domain worldwide.

songs.title: Happy Birthday to You
songs.attribution: Melody by Mildred J. Hill and Patty S. Hill ("Good Morning to All", 1893); the birthday words are traditional. A 2016 US court ruling confirmed the song is in the public domain.

songs.title: Hava Nagila
songs.attribution: Melody: a Hasidic nigun (Sadigura, 19th century), arranged by Abraham Zvi Idelsohn (died 1938), who also wrote the words in 1918 (published in Sefer Hashirim, 1922). Public domain. The raised 7th (F#) of the Jewish "Ahava Rabbah" mode is expected to show as out-of-key.

songs.title: Home on the Range
songs.attribution: Words by Dr. Brewster Higley (1872, as "My Western Home") and tune by Daniel E. Kelley (1873), first printed in the Smith County Pioneer, Kansas, in 1873; public domain worldwide.

songs.title: House of the Rising Sun
songs.attribution: Traditional American folk ballad from Appalachia, first recorded by Clarence Ashley in 1933 and sung by Georgia Turner to Alan Lomax in 1937; this is the plain traditional tune and the traditional words, not any later commercial arrangement, so both are public domain worldwide.

songs.title: CHRISTMAS AVEC TOI
songs.attribution: "CHRISTMAS AVEC TOI" by I'M FRESH! YOU'RE PRETTY!, licensed CC BY 4.0. Recording from Jamendo (https://www.jamendo.com/track/1173749/christmas-avec-toi/lyrics); word timings from the JamendoLyrics dataset.

songs.title: Jingle Bells
songs.attribution: Words and music by James Lord Pierpont, published as "One Horse Open Sleigh" in 1857; public domain worldwide.

songs.title: Joy to the World
songs.attribution: Words by Isaac Watts (1719, from Psalm 98); tune "Antioch" by Lowell Mason (1839/1848), after themes by Handel. Both are public domain worldwide.

songs.title: Kalinka
songs.attribution: Words and music by Ivan Petrovich Larionov (1830-1889), written in 1860 for a Saratov theatre production; public domain. The slow verse ("Akh, pod sosnoyu") is written at the same tempo with its original note values.

songs.title: Le musée d'air contemporain
songs.attribution: "Le musée d'air contemporain" by KPTN, licensed CC BY 4.0. Recording from Jamendo (https://www.jamendo.com/track/1839762/le-musee-d-air-contemporain/lyrics); word timings from the JamendoLyrics dataset.

songs.title: Kumbaya
songs.attribution: African-American spiritual from the southern United States, first recorded and published in 1926; melody and words are anonymous and public domain.

songs.title: La Cucaracha
songs.attribution: Traditional Mexican corrido, sung since the 19th century and popularised during the Mexican Revolution (published in the 1910s); melody and words are anonymous and public domain. The innocuous "patitas" chorus is used.

songs.title: Les files d'attente
songs.attribution: "Les files d'attente" by LAW', licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Recording from Jamendo (https://www.jamendo.com/track/964535/les-files-d-attente/lyrics); word timings from the JamendoLyrics dataset.

songs.title: Mère nature
songs.attribution: "Mère nature" by LAW', licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Recording from Jamendo (https://www.jamendo.com/track/964542/mere-nature/lyrics); word timings from the JamendoLyrics dataset.

songs.title: Loch Lomond
songs.attribution: Traditional Scottish song ("The Bonnie Banks o' Loch Lomond"), first published in Vocal Melodies of Scotland (1841); melody and words are public domain worldwide.

songs.title: Fantasma
songs.attribution: "Fantasma" by LOS ROMBOS, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Recording from Jamendo (https://www.jamendo.com/track/1551324/fantasma/lyrics); word timings from the JamendoLyrics dataset.

songs.title: Is It Right?
songs.attribution: "Is It Right?" by Lower Loveday, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Recording from Jamendo (https://www.jamendo.com/track/1559614/is-it-right); word timings from the JamendoLyrics dataset.

songs.title: Michael, Row the Boat Ashore
songs.attribution: African-American spiritual from the Sea Islands of Georgia, first published in Slave Songs of the United States (1867); anonymous, public domain.

songs.title: Mo Li Hua (Jasmine Flower)
songs.attribution: Traditional Chinese folk song from the Jiangsu region, known since the 18th century (Qianlong era) and first printed in the West by John Barrow in 1804; melody and words are anonymous and public domain. Pentatonic (D E F# A B).

songs.title: Molly Malone
songs.attribution: Words and music by James Yorkston of Edinburgh, published in 1883 (Francis Brothers and Day, London); public domain worldwide.

songs.title: Esencia
songs.attribution: "Esencia" by NANDOMALO, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Recording from Jamendo (https://www.jamendo.com/track/1348566/esencia/lyrics); word timings from the JamendoLyrics dataset.

songs.title: O Tannenbaum (O Christmas Tree)
songs.attribution: Melody: German folk tune (printed 1799, from the student song "Lauriger Horatius"); words by Ernst Anschütz (1824), after Joachim August Zarnack (1819). Both are public domain worldwide. (The familiar English "how lovely are thy branches" text has no verifiable pre-1930 author, so the original German words are used here.)

songs.title: Ode to Joy (Joyful, Joyful, We Adore Thee)
songs.attribution: Melody: the "Ode to Joy" theme from Beethoven's Symphony No. 9 (1824); English hymn words "Joyful, joyful, we adore Thee" by Henry van Dyke (1907). Both are public domain worldwide.

songs.title: Oh! Susanna
songs.attribution: Words and music by Stephen Foster, first published in 1848 (Foster died in 1864), so both are public domain worldwide; only the first verse and the chorus are used.

songs.title: Row, Row, Row Your Boat
songs.attribution: Traditional American nursery round; the words were printed in 1852 and the familiar tune (attributed to Eliphalet Oram Lyte) in 1881. Public domain worldwide.

songs.title: Bad Side
songs.attribution: "Bad Side" by Rxbyn, licensed CC BY 4.0. Recording from Jamendo (https://www.jamendo.com/track/1556580/bad-side); word timings from the JamendoLyrics dataset.

songs.title: Sakura Sakura
songs.attribution: Edo-period koto melody, first printed in the Ministry of Education's Sokyoku-shu (1888); verse 1 is the 1941 "noyama mo sato mo" text (Uta no Hon), verse 2 the 1888 "yayoi no sora wa" text. Anonymous, public domain. The tune uses the Japanese "in" pentatonic scale (A B C E F); the F is expected to show as out-of-key.

songs.title: Santa Lucia
songs.attribution: Traditional Neapolitan barcarolle, published with Teodoro Cottrau's Italian words by the Cottrau firm in Naples in 1849 (Cottrau died 1879); public domain. The F# in "l'onda" is a chromatic passing note in the original.

songs.title: Scarborough Fair
songs.attribution: Traditional English ballad (Child 2, descended from "The Elfin Knight", printed from the 17th century); the melody is the traditional Yorkshire tune in the Dorian mode; words and tune are public domain worldwide.

songs.title: She'll Be Coming 'Round the Mountain
songs.attribution: Traditional American folk song derived from the spiritual "When the Chariot Comes"; first printed in 1899 (Carl Sandburg collected it in 1927). Public domain worldwide.

songs.title: Shenandoah
songs.attribution: Traditional American river song of the early 19th century, first printed in 1876 (Capt. Robert Chamblet Adams) and in Harper's in 1882; melody and words are public domain worldwide.

songs.title: Silent Night
songs.attribution: Melody by Franz Xaver Gruber (1818) to Joseph Mohr's "Stille Nacht"; English words by John Freeman Young (1859). Both are public domain worldwide.

songs.title: Swing Low, Sweet Chariot
songs.attribution: Spiritual attributed to Wallace Willis, a Choctaw freedman, before 1862, first published in the Fisk Jubilee Singers' Jubilee Songs (1873); melody and words are public domain worldwide.

songs.title: The First Noel
songs.attribution: Traditional Cornish/English carol; words and tune first printed by Davies Gilbert (1823) and William Sandys (1833). Public domain worldwide.

songs.title: The Water Is Wide
songs.attribution: Traditional British folk song ("O Waly, Waly", 18th century), collected and published by Cecil Sharp in Folk Songs from Somerset (1906, Sharp died 1924); melody and words are anonymous and public domain.

songs.title: Twinkle, Twinkle, Little Star
songs.attribution: Melody: the French folk tune "Ah! vous dirai-je, maman" (18th century). Words: Jane Taylor, "The Star" (1806). Public domain.

songs.title: Waltzing Matilda
songs.attribution: Words by A. B. "Banjo" Paterson (1864-1941), written in 1895; tune by Christina Macpherson (1864-1936), adapted from the Scottish "Craigielee" (the familiar Marie Cowan arrangement, 1903). All authors died more than 70 years ago; public domain.

songs.title: We Wish You a Merry Christmas
songs.attribution: Traditional West Country (English) carol, words and tune from oral tradition; Arthur Warrell's 1935 arrangement made it popular, but the tune and words themselves are traditional and public domain.

songs.title: When the Saints Go Marching In
songs.attribution: Traditional American spiritual; the familiar tune and words were first recorded in 1923 (Paramount Jubilee Singers) and printed as a traditional song in 1927, so both are public domain worldwide.

songs.title: Yankee Doodle
songs.attribution: Anglo-American tune and words from the 18th century (the "macaroni" verse was in print by the 1780s); public domain worldwide.
